subject.title: [Feature]: Bedrock provider should support guardrail input tagging (guardContent) so Prompt-attack filter doesn't false-block on the system prompt

question: Should configured Bedrock guardrails default to selective evaluation of classified untrusted content, with an explicit compatible all-content mode for operators who require the existing whole-request scan?
rationale: The implementation must choose a security boundary for retrieved and tool-derived content and may change existing guardrail coverage for configured users; source evidence alone cannot determine the intended operator contract.

options.title: Selective default with explicit all-content mode
options.body: Use Bedrock selective tags for user and classified external content by default, while retaining a documented opt-in mode that scans the whole request.

options.title: Keep whole-request scanning by default
options.body: Preserve current guardrail coverage and add selective tagging only as an explicit operator-selected mode.

options.title: Defer pending a generic trust-classification seam
options.body: Pause provider-specific work until maintainers define a shared classification contract for system, user, retrieved, and tool content.

recommendation.title: Selective default with explicit all-content mode
recommendation.body: Use Bedrock selective tags for user and classified external content by default, while retaining a documented opt-in mode that scans the whole request.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository history could not be read in this review environment, so assigning a specific provider-area owner would be speculative.
